verifications.claim: Apollo 13 reached 248,655 miles (400,171 km) from Earth on April 15, 1970.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'At pericynthion on April 15, 1970, 00:21:00 UTC... 400,171 kilometers (248,655 mi) from Earth'; R5: '400,171km (248,655 miles)... set by Apollo 13 in April 1970'; R9: '400,171-kilometer mark... Apollo 13 set in 1970'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact distance and date of April 15, 1970, at pericynthion.

verifications.claim: Apollo 13 held the record for the farthest distance humans have traveled from Earth from April 1970 until April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'beat Apollo 13's record... since 1970'; R3: 'previous record... set in 1970 by Apollo 13'; R4: 'record... until Artemis II's lunar flyby in 2026'; R5: 'surpassed... record of 400,171km... set by Apollo 13 in April 1970'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm Apollo 13 set the record in April 1970, broken by Artemis II in April 2026.

verifications.claim: Apollo 13 set the distance record while using the Moon's gravity to return the crew safely following a critical oxygen tank explosion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'looped around the Moon... oxygen tank... exploded'; R9: 'Apollo 13... long way around the Moon'; R10: 'use the moon's gravity to help return them safely to Earth'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe using Moon's gravity for return after oxygen tank explosion, setting the record.

verifications.claim: Apollo 13 mission lasted 5 days, 22 hours, 54 minutes, and 41 seconds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Mission duration 5 days, 22 hours, 54 minutes, 41 seconds'; R6: '5 Days, 22 Hours, 54 Minutes, 41 Seconds'; R10: matches exactly
verifications.reasoning: Exact duration confirmed in multiple official sources.

verifications.claim: Apollo 13 crew set a record for weight loss during an Apollo flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'set a record that stood up throughout Apollo... nearly 50 percent more than any other crew'
verifications.reasoning: NASA source directly states they set the Apollo weight loss record.

verifications.claim: Apollo 13 crew lost a total of 31.5 pounds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'the crew lost a total of 31.5 pounds'; R4: 'lost a total of 14 kilograms (31 lb)'
verifications.reasoning: Exact total confirmed; 14kg ≈31lb, precise in R10.

verifications.claim: Jack Swigert was the Command Module Pilot of Apollo 13.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Jack Swigert as command module (CM) pilot'; R6: 'John L. Swigert, Jr., Command Module Pilot'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently identified as CMP across sources.

verifications.claim: Jack Swigert stepped in last minute.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Swigert was a late replacement... two days before launch'; R6: 'Swigert replaced... pre-flight substitution'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm last-minute replacement for Mattingly.

verifications.claim: Jack Swigert set a personal record for longest time in space at the time, along with crewmates Jim Lovell and Fred Haise.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No sources mention any crew setting a longest time in space record; Lovell had prior longer missions (Gemini 7: 14 days), Apollo 13 ~6 days.

verifications.claim: Apollo 13 distance record stood for over 56 years until it was broken by the Artemis II mission on April 6, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'set the new mark on Monday (April 6)'; R3: 'April 6, 2026'; R1: 'April 6, 2026 at 4:16 PM PDT Artemis II sets a new record'

verifications.claim: Apollo 13 mission was originally planned as the third lunar landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'would have been the third Moon landing'; R7: 'third lunar landing attempt'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as planned third lunar landing.

verifications.claim: Apollo 13 mission became a rescue mission after an explosion in the Service Module's number two oxygen tank
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'oxygen tank in the service module (SM) exploded... number 2 oxygen tank'; R10: 'rupture of service module oxygen tank No. 2'
verifications.reasoning: Exact details match: SM oxygen tank #2 explosion led to abort/rescue.
